properties.name: FIELD REPORT (hxm_program hub, 2026-09-14, v0.60.2): asked for a management progress deck, the agent asserted project status from a file checklist and its own recent writes, never reading the design; challenged, one topic call gave 20 hits across 9 node types, and it had known 6 of 41 change events
properties.statement:
RELAYED by Anthony from hxm_program, a hub or project-brain design spanning many inter-related projects, 2026-09-14, against reflow2 v0.60.2. Anthony's question to that session, verbatim: "why didn't you use the reflow2 graph to see what status was available for the project? It seemed that once you did, you found a whole bunch of status that you didn't think about at first." The session's own account is filed in that project's feedback file as items F-22 to F-25 and O-13 to O-16.

STEP 1 - THE OBSERVATION, no diagnosis. The user asked for a progress deck for management. The agent produced status claims from (a) a script-by-script checklist file that the project's house rules point at, whose boxes are unticked by convention rather than by measurement, and (b) the six change events it had itself written that week. It did not read the design first. Expected: a status assertion about a design under reflow2 is read from the design before it is written. Not affected: the same agent's finding records that month opened the root-cause skill three times when demanded, so a demand on a tool does reach it.

TWO THINGS THAT SESSION MEASURED rather than assumed, after the challenge:
- topic_report existed, was the right tool, and returned 20 hits across 9 node types in ONE call, including the project node, the accepted top-level requirement and five capabilities with statuses. The agent did not know it was there. It is keyword-only: it found the project node and did not offer to expand it, so it still missed the monochromator and every upstream contribution, which were the two things the user named (recorded separately on the topic capability).
- changelog_view returned ZERO entries from 41 dated change events, because the design has no deployed release and the window never opens. A second sighting, in a different setting, of fact:changelog-view-is-step-two-of-the-cut-and-returns-nothing-for-a-real-cut.

THE SESSION'S OWN RANKED CANDIDATE CAUSES, recorded as candidates and not as a verdict; the root-cause walk is owed and has not been run here:
1. The orientation skill (where-am-i) is worded for a different audience: it triggers on the USER asking where things stand or picking a design back up. "Produce a progress deck" was never mapped onto "read the design first". A clause saying the audience is not the trigger would have caught it.
2. Nothing demanded the read at the moment of the claim. A finding record demands the root-cause skill and that fired three times that month; there is no equivalent guard on "the agent is about to assert what this project has achieved", partly because no tool call marks that moment. This is the class fact:the-root-cause-skill-is-demanded-by-no-tool-and-named-by-no-trigger-so-it-loads-only-by-luck names in its step 6, with a SECOND member: a trigger defined by the agent's internal state (about to assert status) rather than by an observable act.
3. A file surface looked authoritative and was actively misleading: a plan was read and reported as a measurement.
4. Recency bias nothing could see: writing into the graph all week felt like knowing the project. Every existing signal measures what the agent owes the graph; nothing measures what the graph has not yet told the agent.

WHAT THE SESSION PROPOSED, recorded as ideas beside this finding and not as intent: reading coverage ("you have read 6 of the 41 change events touching this"), and a project-scoped status rollup using the scope detect_gaps already takes. Its own ranking: reading coverage first, because the failure was confident partial knowledge, not absent tooling.

WHY THE SUBJECT IS THE TRIGGER MACHINERY: the tool that would have answered exists and is served; the skill that would have prompted the read exists and is served; what was absent is anything that keys the read to the moment a status claim is about to be written. The same shape as the wall check finding of 2026-09-14: the legs a consumer needs are the served tool, the instruction at the moment of use, and a detector that notices the absence.
